question:
**Fill in the Blank:**

Panthi dance is linked to the followers of ______ in Chhattisgarh.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Guru Ghasidas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Panthi dance** is a traditional folk dance form closely associated with the followers of Guru Ghasidas in Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is performed as a devotional tribute to Guru Ghasidas, who founded the **Satnami sect**, emphasizing equality, truth, and social justice.
 
• The dance is characterized by spiritual songs and rhythmic movements, portraying the teachings of Guru Ghasidas and the values of the Satnami sect.
 
• Panthi dance holds great cultural significance in Chhattisgarh, particularly during festive occasions such as **Maghi Purnima**, which marks the birth anniversary of Guru Ghasidas.
 
• The performers use expressive gestures, devotional hymns, and synchronized movements to narrate stories of Guru Ghasidas' life and his efforts to promote social harmony.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kabir**

 
 
• Kabir was a 15th-century Indian mystic poet and saint whose teachings emphasized devotion to one God and rejected idol worship.
 
• He inspired the **Kabir Panth**, a religious movement based on his philosophy of universal love and unity.
 
• Kabir's poetry, including dohas (couplets), is widely studied for its spiritual depth and social relevance.
 
 
 
• **Kabuli**
 
 
• The term "Kabuli" generally refers to people or things originating from Kabul, Afghanistan.
 
• It is not directly related to any specific dance or cultural tradition in Chhattisgarh.
 
 
 
• **Nanak**
 
 
• Guru Nanak was the founder of Sikhism and the first Sikh Guru, whose teachings focused on equality, truth, and devotion to one God.
 
• His philosophy inspired the formation of a distinct religious community, and his hymns are included in the Guru Granth Sahib.
